sources.parallel_text: line-aligned mzr<->por: 3,951 row pairs / 10,302 mzr tokens (extracted 2026-10-18)
sources.extraction_note: Portuguese column repaired deterministically (408 repairs: cedilla markers, nasal diphthongs, footnote superscripts incl. spaced and quote-adjacent markers); Marubo column is NOT repairable from this scan: the OCR drops the printed nasality marks (Awẽ nimẽaitõ -> Awe nimeaito, inĩki -> inlki) and mixes tilde/macron conventions. 80.7% of rows carry at least one unattested mzr token; 753 rows (19.1%) screen clean. Shipped as alignment evidence in exports/parallel_candidates/ (outside the dataset glob), not as training data. Unblock with a clean digital transcription, not re-OCR.
sources.register: ritual_restricted review required (ADR-0025: metadata, not a gate)
sources.clean_form_citation_note: 867 of 4,033 rows have their whole token sequence printed with diacritics in born-digital works (Villada Castro 2018, Mundo Amazonico 9(1); Cesarino 2008 thesis, decoded; Cesarino 2018 Wenia as shared-formula only); 606 unanimous citations of which 319 add a nasal mark the scan lost, 191 conflicts kept unresolved, 70 uncorroborated. Cited forms are hypotheses, not validated observations: src is never rewritten. The 2008 UFRJ thesis (cesarino_2008_oniska) is a third quoted-chant reference via its decoded PDF text.

sources.parallel_text: line-aligned mzr<->por: 921 verse rows / 2,401 mzr tokens, PDF pages 15-48 (extracted 2026-10-18)
sources.extraction_note: Born-digital PDF (Producer: Microsoft Word 2010): the text layer is the author's own manuscript, so the Marúbo nasality diacritics (ẽ ĩ ũ ã õ) are intact - unlike the scanned 2013 book. The chant table prints each verse beside its Portuguese translation, numbered every fifth line; extracted from pdftotext -layout, so each row is read out of the source (20.1% of rows keep the printed line number as a locator). 76 Portuguese footnote superscripts stripped deterministically (qc.tgt_raw keeps the raw line); zero residual damage, zero OCR-artefact flags. 87.7% of rows use at least one token absent from the scripture/academic reference vocabulary - that is chant lexicon, not damage, because there is no OCR layer. This is a DIFFERENT chant from the twelve in the 2013 book, so it does not repair the book's OCR.

replication_protocol.step_1: Query academic repositories (Pantheon UFRJ, USP, UFAM, Museu do Índio) for ISO code and language name.
replication_protocol.step_2: Harvest ScriptureEarth USFM text and timed audio if available.
replication_protocol.step_3: Ingest ASJP Swadesh wordlists and Glottolog bibliography.
replication_protocol.step_4: Record governance policy for each source in sources_index.json before pipeline extraction.
replication_protocol.step_5: Run Langpipe citation miner and valence induction on harvested parallel segments.

policy_basis: ADR-0025: a source present in var/external/ is authorized for processing and training; licence and ownership are records, not gates. Entries here that carry `exclude` or `review_required` are research triage for indexed (not yet acquired) leads, not licence gates; once a source is downloaded into the repository, presence authorizes it and the policy is `direct` unless the operator explicitly excludes it.
